film: THE OBSERVER — The Man Who Could Not Be Read (Film II)
note: The mythic continuation of THE MOMENT, rendered in a Nolan/Joker gray-shade register. This film uses NO real photographs of Kunal: the protagonist is a wholly separate, invented, machine-augmented figure whose reference stills are GENERATED by src/forge_character.py (no user photos to source). Non-linear structure: the present creature, the midnight birth (continuation of Film I's last frame), the coma + machine-augmentation years, and the mirror. Original monologues only (no borrowed Joker lines). Original score only (no licensed songs).

globals.tone: high-contrast expressionist cinema in the tradition of Christopher Nolan and Roger Deakins; IMAX-scale nocturnal atmosphere, anamorphic wide lensing, dramatic chiaroscuro with a single hard motivated key light carving the subject out of deep blacks; volumetric haze, rain-sheen on every surface, monumental negative space with the figure often small against vast architecture; slow deliberate camera, patient push-ins and craning reveals; a mythic, dreamlike unreality, brooding, majestic and severe; painterly darkness, photoreal, fine film grain, highly detailed, cinematic color grade; NOT cheerful, NOT comedic

observer.summary: A wholly invented, separate character — NOT Kunal's likeness. A tall, gaunt, aged man in his late 40s–50s: weathered skin, deep lines, a greying dark beard, hollow cheeks, a once-boyish face now hardened by years. Machine-augmented resurrection: subtle cybernetics, a faint chrome seam tracing the left jaw and temple, a hairline of metal at the neck, one eye faintly luminous (cold pale-blue augmented iris), the other human and dark. Gray-shade Joker register: worn bone-white greasepaint, cracked and imperfect, with a fixed 'stressed smile' painted at the mouth — a strained rictus, NOT a happy grin, NOT circus clown. The greasepaint is concealment, not decoration: beneath it the face was lost to a therapy-machine detonation and rebuilt, so the paint and the chrome half-hide old ruin where flesh was erased (always suggested in shadow, never shown graphically). Costume: a long, dark, weathered high-collared coat, an iconic monumental silhouette. Dignified, severe, unreadable.
